# President Trump Names Stephen Miller as 33rd White House Chief of Staff

President Donald J. Trump announced the appointment of Stephen Miller as the 33rd White House Chief of Staff, succeeding Susie Wiles after her tenure in the role.

Miller has served alongside President Trump since the beginning and has been instrumental in the Administration's major successes, including driving violent crime to historic lows, securing the border at unprecedented levels, and dismantling large-scale fraud. He brings deep experience, broad institutional knowledge, and unwavering commitment to the role.

## Statements of Support

Vice President JD Vance expressed gratitude to Wiles, stating: "Stephen Miller is an amazing patriot and will do great things."

Secretary of State Marco Rubio praised Wiles' service and noted: "I look forward to continuing to work with Stephen Miller, one of the President's most trusted and longtime advisors."

Attorney General Todd Blanche commented: "Together we've reduced crime to historic levels, enhanced public safety throughout our communities."

Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation Kash Patel remarked: "Stephen has been a friend and colleague since the first Trump administration."

Former White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt described Miller as: "No one is more loyal, more hardworking, or more in touch with the America First movement."

Heritage Foundation President Kevin Roberts stated: "His appointment as chief of staff signals that the Trump administration is not rolling over to the radical Left."
